obj.NEW_CUSTOMER_body: Turn people who installed or registered into first-time buyers.
obj.LAPSED_REACTIVATION_body: Bring back customers who stopped ordering 30–60 days ago, before they are lost.
obj.RETENTION_body: Keep active customers ordering, using next-order rewards instead of deep discounts.
obj.LOYALTY_REWARD_body: Thank loyal customers with wallet credit or a free extra on milestone orders.
obj.FREQUENT_ORDER_body: Reward customers who order often: a stamp card, an order challenge or order milestones.
obj.FIRST_ORDER_body: Give customers with no orders a simple reason to place the first one.
obj.REPEAT_PURCHASE_body: Turn customers who ordered once into repeat customers: the biggest drop-off point.
obj.SPECIFIC_ITEM_body: Launch a new dish or move a high-margin item.
obj.MIN_ORDER_VALUE_body: Grow basket size: set the minimum 15–30% above today’s average order.
obj.UPSELL_body: Add a side, drink or dessert to the basket at a small price.
obj.PICKUP_body: Shift orders to pickup, which costs less than delivery.
obj.DELIVERY_body: Remove the delivery fee, the most common reason people leave at checkout.
obj.SLOW_HOURS_body: Fill the afternoon lull and quiet weekdays.
obj.NEW_BRANCH_body: Introduce a new branch to the people around it.
obj.OCCASION_body: A gift on the customer’s day, National Day, Ramadan and Eid.
obj.SERVICE_RECOVERY_body: Win back a customer after a bad experience, with a coupon they did not expect.

groups.loyalBody: Ordered 4+ times in 90 days. Reward, never discount.
groups.highValueBody: Top 10% by spend. Cashback keeps them.
groups.atRiskBody: Used to order often; 30–60 days quiet.
groups.lostBody: No order in 60+ days. A fixed amount works best.
groups.title: Customer groups
groups.desc: Who is loyal, who is at risk, who is lost, and the goal that fits each group.

perf.title: Performance
perf.desc: Return on cost = extra profit minus the campaign cost, measured against the customers who did not get the coupon.
perf.onTrack: studied campaigns on track (≥80% of planned profit)
perf.waitingLessons: finished campaigns waiting for lessons learned
perf.liabilityCaption: unused value customers can still redeem
perf.resultsDesc: Every measured campaign: what it cost, what it brought, and whether it created orders that would not have happened.
perf.planDesc: The forecast fixed at approval beside what actually happened. A campaign is on track above 80% of its planned profit.
perf.noPlan: No campaign with an approved forecast yet.
perf.lessonGreat: Strong return - repeat it on the same segment; try a smaller discount next time to test the floor.
perf.lessonOk: Paid for itself. The extra orders were modest: narrow the audience to the customers who actually responded.
perf.lessonLoss: A loss: most redeemers would have ordered anyway. Use a smaller amount, a higher minimum order, or a tighter segment.
perf.evalDesc: Lessons for next time, one per finished campaign.

settings.desc: The business rules every campaign is checked against, and who may create and approve.
settings.fourEyesV: The person who creates a campaign cannot approve it
settings.liveCampaignsV: {{f}} are locked once customers hold the coupon
settings.rulesNote: These rules are part of the engine. Changing them needs development (see the field specification).
settings.canApproveV: Roles with “Approve marketing work”, except their own campaigns
settings.engineLive: Live - Yiji v2 through the CRM gateway.
settings.engineSample: Sample data - until Yiji v2 is connected.
settings.engineHow: To go live: the gateway gets MARKETING_ENGINE_URL and MARKETING_ENGINE_KEY, then the Administrator sets the global setting “marketing_engine” to “live”. No release needed.
settings.sampleRestored: Sample campaigns restored - reload the page.
settings.brandsStoresV: Menus, items and branches come from the engine’s catalogue.
settings.stackingDesc: Coupons have three compatibility settings. Each is set per coupon and checked by the engine on every order, so the app cannot be used to get around them.
settings.stackingPolicy: Stacking policy - one order, every product
settings.s1b: App offers such as 20% off or free delivery apply first, to the order subtotal.
settings.s2b: One coupon per order unless the coupon allows other discounts. Applied to what is left after the offer.
settings.s3b: Points, cashback or VIP benefits apply last among discounts, if the coupon allows loyalty.
settings.s4b: Pays the remaining amount. It is a payment method, not a discount, so it never blocks a coupon unless the gift card product says so.
settings.changeInStep4: Change these in each coupon, step 4 (Eligibility).
settings.brandsDesc: {{n}} items from the engine’s menu catalogue. These are the items coupons can include, exclude, give free or bundle.
settings.fieldsDesc: Generated from the same schema that drives the campaign form, so it always matches. {{n}} fields in 7 steps. Times are Saudi time (Asia/Riyadh).
settings.archDesc: What Yiji v2 provides and how this portal reaches it. Today: {{e}}.
settings.engineSampleShort: the sample engine in this browser
settings.svcEngineV: checkout validation, redemptions, the value ledger, issuance, the catalogue.
settings.svcPortalV: studies, campaign set-up, approvals, performance, gift cards and rewards management, settings.
settings.svcGatewayV: the only path to the engine; checks the person may use the portal, adds the engine key, forwards 1:1.
settings.svcRolesV: Prepare marketing work (create), Approve marketing work (approve, never one’s own), managed by the Administrator.
settings.gl1: Yiji v2 exposes the endpoints below with a service key for the CRM.
settings.gl2: The CRM gateway gets MARKETING_ENGINE_URL and MARKETING_ENGINE_KEY (staging first).
settings.gl3: The Administrator sets the global setting “marketing_engine” to “live”.
settings.gl4: Open Home: the “Sample data” badge is gone and the numbers are Yiji’s.
